To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rigid body co-registration is an acceptable basis of motion correction, provided that correlation analysis is done using a variance measure.

(1) the use of a variance estimator in correlation analysis is important for the detection of motion artifacts; (2) the use of rigid body co-registering for the correction of motion artifacts is acceptable provided a variance estimator is used in the correlation analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of rigid body co-registrations in fMRI analysis.
the problem of residual motion artifacts in fMRI analysis.
the statistical analysis of fMRI data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a measure of variance in the estimation of the correlation coefficient is a good basis for fMRI analysis.
, in the absence of a more sophisticated approach, correlation analysis using variance estimates from the data at the voxel level is the most appropriate method for fMRI analysis.
rigid body co-registration is a useful first step in the analysis of parametric fMRI data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of rigid body co-registraion for fMRI data is a reasonable approach, but that it should be used in conjunction with an appropriate measure of correlation.
correlation based on the covariance matrix is not robust to motion and that correlation based on a voxel-wise estimate of variance is a better alternative.
rigid body co-registration is a reasonable basis for re-aligment of fMRI data sets, but that correlation analysis is a more sensitive method for detecting motion artifacts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
motion artifacts are a significant issue in fMRI analysis.
motion artifacts can be detected and visualised in correlation based fMRI analysis.
the visualisation of residual motion effects is a useful way of assessing the quality of fMRI data and that it should be incorporated into any analysis package.
